sections.title: QIB Jahiz — One Click Finance pre-approval readiness and remediation platform

items.title: Design document · v2 · 7–8 October 2026 · Cognirise for Qatar Islamic Bank (QIB)

Status: v1 (sections 1–18) was the design for approval; the v2 addendum (sections 19–23) records the build decisions taken on 8 October: no QIB answers needed (everything is a setting), the customer channel, the Demo Director, and what ships.
Product name
items.body: Jahiz (جاهز, "ready"): the platform's job is to make customers ready for One Click Finance again. Agents carry Arabic names in the same way as Rafeeq (Tasama HR) and Mizan.

items.title: Markers
items.body: [Q] stated by QIB (through Mounir's brief) · [R] research-sourced — a regulation, a published rule or a documented practice, with the source in research/01-… and research/02-… · [D] our design decision · [A] assumption that QIB must confirm. Every number in a policy table is either [R] or a design default; design defaults are editable on the Policies screen, so QIB's answers replace values, not design. Where the research itself marks a point UNVERIFIED, this document says so.

sections.title: What the research says, in one page

items.title: The problem as QIB states it.
items.body: QIB pre-approves existing customers for a finance limit and pushes an app notification ("One Click Finance"); the customer accepts, passes a set of approvals and e-signatures, and the finance is disbursed into the account. Only 35% of customers qualify through the pre-approval model. The other 65% fall out for the twenty reasons QIB has ranked by frequency (section 3). Today QIB reviews customer lists monthly and takes manual action per situation. QIB has been asked for the action list its policy prescribes per reason; it is not yet in hand.

items.title: What One Click Finance is, publicly.
items.body: Launched 28 November 2018 as "Instant Finance", described by QIB as the first fully digital end-to-end personal financing by an Islamic bank: eligible customers are notified by SMS and/or app notification, choose the amount, confirm, e-sign and receive funds within minutes. In November 2024 QIB said AI-based credit risk models "enable pre-approval for the award-winning One Click finance". Eligibility stated on qib.com.qa: salary credited to a QIB account; or a fixed-deposit holder; or an existing finance customer for top-ups. 83% of QIB retail customers are digitally active (2023). (research/01 §6)

items.title: The rules the pre-approval model has to respect.
items.body: QCB retail-credit limits trace to the April 2011 directive and no change to them was found since: Qatari nationals QAR 2,000,000 over 72 months, expatriates QAR 400,000 over 48 months, both including profit; monthly instalment ≤ 75% of salary (Qataris) or 50% (expatriates). The base — "basic salary + social allowance" for Qataris, "total salary" for residents — is how QIB's and Ahlibank's pages state it; the QCB text itself could not be fetched, so the base wording is UNVERIFIED against the primary source. QIB's own page adds: Qataris 18–65, residents 21–60 (whether measured at maturity is not stated — Ahlibank's page says "at maturity"), employment with a QIB-approved employer, salary certificate, valid QID (or residence permit + passport), minimum finance QAR 15,000 for the branch product. QIB's One Click minimum is QAR 5,000. Credit Bureau reports require the customer's prior consent and keep dishonoured cheques for three years from settlement. Bounced cheques remain a criminal offence in Qatar (Penal Code art. 357); Law 1/2024 added mandatory partial payment. (research/01 §1, §4, §6)

items.title: What the law says about contacting customers.
items.body: Law 13/2016 (PDPPL) art. 22 and the CRA Spam Regulation art. 6: no direct marketing without prior consent; no direct marketing between 21:00 and 09:00; opt-out must take effect within two business days; sender identified in Arabic and English; consent is presumed for messages relevant to an existing relationship when an easy opt-out is offered. QCB issued a Data Handling and Protection Regulation in February 2025; vendor summaries describe explicit consent, separate marketing consent and a retention policy, but the text itself was not reachable (UNVERIFIED). The design treats service and regulatory messages ("your QID has expired") as not marketing and a pre-approved offer as marketing. That distinction is inferred from the CRA's existing-relationship presumption and from UK ICO guidance on regulatory communications; it must be confirmed against the NCSA direct-marketing guideline (PDPPL-02050218E), which exists but could not be read. It runs through the whole policy model (section 4). (research/01 §2–3; research/02 §1.3)

items.title: What other regulators prescribe for the parameters QIB has not given us. Contact frequency
items.body: SAMA ≤ 10 phone attempts per 30 days; ACCC/ASIC 3 calls/week, 10/month; CFPB Reg F 7 calls in 7 days as an upper bound. Hours: CBUAE collections 09:00–20:00; UAE marketing calls 09:00–18:00. Expired ID: CBUAE requires written notices and a 90-calendar-day notice period before a temporary card block (branch operations continue, no fee); SAMA requires 30 days' notice before freezing on ID expiry; RBI requires at least three advance and three post-due intimations including one letter. KYC refresh cycles: 1/2/3 years by risk (CBUAE), with a trend toward trigger-based review (Wolfsberg 2022). No regulator prescribes the T-90/-60/-30 pre-expiry cadence; it is practice, and we adopt it as a design default. (research/02 §1–2)

items.title: Segments. QIB's public tiers are Private Banking (by invitation; relationship value not disclosed), Tamayuz (QAR 350,000 average deposits or QAR 50,000 monthly salary; dedicated…
items.body: Segments. QIB's public tiers are Private Banking (by invitation; relationship value not disclosed), Tamayuz (QAR 350,000 average deposits or QAR 50,000 monthly salary; dedicated RM) and Essential. Mounir's four value segments map onto them: VVIP = Private Banking · HNWI = upper Tamayuz · High Value = Tamayuz threshold and affluent salaried · Mass = Essential. No regulator requires HNWI communications to route through the RM; private-banking service models do, and we make RM-first a per-segment policy switch. (research/01 §6; research/02 §6)

items.title: Status flags and cautionary notes.
items.body: No public QCB taxonomy exists. Documented Qatari practice: accounts blocked on employer termination notice / end-of-service payment or on an unpaid instalment (CBQ), blocked when no QID is presented within 90 days (QNB, "as per QCB policy"), closed on death/incapacity/bankruptcy/arrest, frozen by court order (Judicial Enforcement Law 4/2024; lifts on a discharge certificate) or sanctions designation (lifts only on delisting). Dormancy after one year without transactions on current accounts (HSBC Qatar's disclosures; the QCB instruction is UNVERIFIED). Only KYC-expired, salary-stopped, delinquency and dormant are customer-remediable; the rest need an external event. (research/01 §5, §8)

items.title: What this means for the design.
items.body: The gap is not the credit model and not the app journey — both exist. The gap is the remediation layer between the monthly list and the customer: knowing which fall-outs a customer can cure, asking for exactly the evidence that cures them inside the law's contact limits, reading what comes back, updating the record under maker-checker control, and putting the customer back in front of the pre-approval model without waiting for next month's review. Jahiz is that layer. It does not decide credit; it makes the data the credit model needs true, current and complete.

sections.title: What is deliberately not in scope

items.title: The pre-approval credit model itself and the risk cut-off.
items.body: Jahiz runs a deterministic eligibility check that mirrors the QCB/QIB rules so it can explain fall-outs and re-check cures; the bank's model remains the decision-maker. The model's output is simulated.

items.title: The One Click Finance journey in the QIB app (offer → approvals → e-sign → disbursement).
items.body: Jahiz hands a re-qualified customer back to it; the hand-off is simulated.

items.title: Collections beyond early arrears.
items.body: Jahiz sends pre-delinquency reminders inside the collections policy and hands cases over at the policy's DPD boundary; it is not a collections system.

items.title: Sanctions, fraud and legal processes.
items.body: Cautionary notes of those kinds are routed to Compliance and never remediated by customer contact.

items.title: Real channel delivery (SMTP, SMS gateway, push, WhatsApp).
items.body: The prototype simulates every channel end to end and shows the customer's view of each message; adapters are stubbed.

items.title: Authentication, SSO, entitlements, production audit retention.
items.body: Personas are a switcher, not authentication.

sections.title: Scope and the five questions the demo must answer

items.title: Jahiz sits on top of a simulated QIB customer database full of synthetic data (section 10–11) and has to answer, on screen, in this order:
"Of the 65% who fall out, how many could be cured by a customer action, how many by a bank action, and how many not at all?"
items.body: the Data health screen: fall-outs by reason, by segment, by class (ask the customer / bank must act / not eligible by policy / collections boundary), with the overlap of multiple reasons and the trend over six months.

items.title: "What is Jahiz doing about it right now, and under which rules?"
items.body: the Cases workspace (Intake → In flight → Output) and the Communications screen: every request, reminder, inbound reply, document and update, each stamped with the policy version and clause that allowed it, and every message that policy *blocked*, with the reason.

items.title: "Did the customer's data actually get fixed, and who approved it?"
items.body: the Documents screen and the customer 360: extraction, verification, the proposed before/after, the checker's decision, and the record update written through the core connector.

items.title: "Is the customer eligible again?"
items.body: the re-qualification result on the case and the customer, with the eligible amount computed under the current eligibility parameters and the hand-off to One Click Finance (simulated push).

items.title: "Can we change the rules without a change request?"
items.body: the Policies screen: per-segment parameters, a versioned change with approval, and the visible effect on the schedule.

items.title: Plus the assistant proof
items.body: ask Dalil anything about the data or the actions ("why is DEMO-C-01842 not eligible?", "how many Tamayuz customers have an expired QID?", "send the second reminder to the three cases waiting on me") and get an answer from the same database the screens use, with the policy clause cited and every write confirmed on screen.

items.title: Every fall-out reason belongs to one of four classes.
items.body: The class decides whether the customer is contacted at all, and by whom.

items.title: A · Ask the customer
items.body: Meaning: The cure is evidence or a decision only the customer can give · Jahiz does: Opens a remediation case, runs the outreach workflow under the segment's contact policy, processes the reply, updates the record, re-qualifies · Customer contact: Yes — service messages, within policy

items.title: B · Bank must act
items.body: Meaning: The cure is a bank decision or process (employer approval, exposure recalculation, cautionary-note review) · Jahiz does: Opens an internal review case in the right queue with the pack prepared; informs the customer only once something changes for them · Customer contact: Only after the bank's decision, and only if policy allows

items.title: C · Not eligible by policy
items.body: Meaning: A hard rule (age, nationality, segment, model cut-off, rating, minimum amount) · Jahiz does: Records the reason, suppresses offers, schedules a re-check on the date or event that could change it · Customer contact: No

items.title: D · Collections boundary
items.body: Meaning: Payment conduct (DPD, irregular payments, returned cheques) · Jahiz does: Suppresses offers, sends early-arrears reminders only inside the collections policy, hands over at the DPD boundary, re-checks after the cooling period · Customer contact: Payment reminders only, under the collections policy

items.title: Rank and reason are QIB's.
items.body: Definitions are design defaults unless marked, because QIB's policy definitions are not yet in hand — every threshold below is a parameter on the Policies screen (section 4). "Agents" are introduced in section 5; "WF" in section 6; "POL" in section 4.

items.title: 1 — Missing / low salary in any of the last 6 months
items.body: Class: A · Definition in Jahiz (default): No credit tagged salary in a calendar month, or a credit below 70% of the trailing 6-month median · Likely causes: Job change; unpaid leave; salary moved to another bank; delayed payroll (two credits next month); employer WPS failure; part-month · What Jahiz does: Service message asking the customer to confirm employment status and upload a salary certificate ≤ 30 days old (sent regardless of marketing consent); if the reply shows salary is paid elsewhere, a salary-transfer offer goes as a separate message only where marketing consent exists, otherwise as an RM/branch task; if employer changed → reason 2 path · Evidence that cures it: Salary certificate; HR letter for unpaid leave; salary-transfer instruction. An explained single gap may be accepted — by Credit Policy for High Value/HNWI/VVIP, by the Operations Supervisor for Mass — if acceptExplainedGap is on; otherwise the case parks until six clean months exist · Agents · WF · POL: Munadi · Mustaqbil · Fahis · Muhaddith · Muahil · WF-04 · POL-03, POL-07 · Re-check: On document; monthly on salary history

items.title: 2 — Employer unapproved or missing
items.body: Class: A (missing) / B (unapproved) · Definition in Jahiz (default): Missing: no employer on record or employer not matched to the register. Unapproved: employer on record but not on QIB's approved list · Likely causes: Data gap from migration; new employer after job change; small or new company; employer never applied for listing · What Jahiz does: Missing: ask the customer for employer details + salary certificate. Unapproved: Muwathiq prepares the employer approval pack (CR, WPS status, sector, headcount, QIB-salaried staff count) for Credit Policy; customers are told only when approved; QIB@work route offered where it fits · Evidence that cures it: Salary certificate naming the employer; Credit Policy decision on the employer · Agents · WF · POL: Munadi · Mustaqbil · Fahis · Muwathiq · Muhaddith · Muahil · WF-05 · POL-03, POL-04 · Re-check: On employer decision — one approval can re-qualify every employee of that employer

items.title: 3 — Exceeds permissible exposure to financing amount
items.body: Class: B · Definition in Jahiz (default): Existing exposure (repayable, incl. profit) ≥ nationality cap (QAR 2m / 400k), or DBR capacity ≤ 0 after existing obligations. Evaluated after reason 4: if removing the counted standing orders would restore capacity, the reason is 4, not 3 · Likely causes: Large home or vehicle finance; cards at limit; buy-out not completed · What Jahiz does: Computes the headroom timeline (when existing facilities mature) and the consolidation case for Credit; no outreach by default (exposureInfoMessage = off, POL-04) · Evidence that cures it: Nothing from the customer; maturity or prepayment · Agents · WF · POL: Raqib · Muahil · WF-11 · POL-04 · Re-check: At each instalment date; on prepayment

items.title: 4 — Standing orders exceed limits
items.body: Class: A · Definition in Jahiz (default): Recurring standing orders to other financial institutions counted as obligations; "exceed" when their total ≥ 25% of salary_total · Likely causes: Other-bank finance repaid by standing order; school fees; family transfers misclassified as commitments · What Jahiz does: In-app message listing the standing orders and asking the customer to classify each (loan repayment / savings / family / other) and, for other-bank finance, to supply a liability letter; checker approves the reclassification; Credit can propose consolidation · Evidence that cures it: Self-declaration; liability letter · Agents · WF · POL: Munadi · Mustaqbil · Fahis · Muhaddith · Muahil · WF-07 · POL-03, POL-04, POL-06 · Re-check: On declaration

items.title: 5 — Has cautionary note
items.body: Class: B · Definition in Jahiz (default): Any active note. Sub-types: KYC-expired; salary-stopped; court attachment; sanctions; fraud/AML; legal hold; deceased · Likely causes: Court order; sanctions screening hit; fraud investigation; death notification; expired KYC flagged by Compliance · What Jahiz does: Every note goes to the Compliance queue with its origin and lifting condition; no customer contact until Compliance acts. Compliance may reclassify a KYC-expired or salary-stopped note to WF-02/03 or WF-04 in one click; the other types stay with Compliance · Evidence that cures it: Compliance clearance; discharge certificate; delisting · Agents · WF · POL: Raqib · Hami · WF-10 · POL-05 · Re-check: On note lift

items.title: 6 — Passport expired
items.body: Class: A · Definition in Jahiz (default): Passport expiry < today (residents; Qataris need no passport for eligibility, POL-04). Separately, a passport expiring within 90 days opens a pre-expiry watch case so the fall-out is prevented — the watch is a trigger, not a reason · Likely causes: Renewal in progress at the embassy; renewed but not uploaded · What Jahiz does: Pre-expiry notices T-90/-60/-30 (watch), then T0, T+30, T+60 (fall-out); upload via app preferred, e-mail accepted for Mass/High Value, RM-collected for HNWI/VVIP; extraction + verification (expiry, name, number, MRZ check digits); maker-checker; record update; re-qualify. At T+90 a proposed temporary restriction goes to the approver the segment policy names · Evidence that cures it: New passport data page · Agents · WF · POL: Munadi · Mustaqbil · Fahis · Muhaddith · Muahil · WF-03 · POL-02, POL-06 · Re-check: On document

items.title: 7 — QID expired
items.body: Class: A · Definition in Jahiz (default): QID expiry < today; a QID expiring within 90 days opens a pre-expiry watch case (trigger, not reason) · Likely causes: Residence permit renewal pending with the employer; renewed card not uploaded · What Jahiz does: As reason 6; QID front and back; the QID number must match the record (a different QID number on the same customer is a flag, not an update) · Evidence that cures it: New QID · Agents · WF · POL: as above · WF-02 · POL-02, POL-06 · Re-check: On document

items.title: 8 — Does not have current account
items.body: Class: A · Definition in Jahiz (default): Customer holds only savings/deposit accounts; One Click disburses into a current account [Q implied] · Likely causes: Deposit-only relationship; current account closed/dormant · What Jahiz does: Where marketing consent exists: in-app offer to open a current account (a product offer). Without consent: Mass cases park awaiting-consent and re-check when consent is recorded; High Value and above get an RM/branch task. A dormant current account → reactivation (reason 13) · Evidence that cures it: Account opened (checker-approved flag through the connector); dormant account reactivated · Agents · WF · POL: Hami · Munadi · Mustaqbil · Muhaddith · Muahil · WF-08 · POL-07, POL-06 · Re-check: On account event; on consent

items.title: 9 — Failed due to risk model cut-off
items.body: Class: C · Definition in Jahiz (default): Bank model score below cut-off; Jahiz holds the score as an opaque input · Likely causes: Model inputs; bureau score · What Jahiz does: Records; suppresses; re-scores monthly; shows the RM (HNWI/VVIP) that the customer is out on model, not on data · Evidence that cures it: None from the customer · Agents · WF · POL: Raqib · WF-14 · POL-04 · Re-check: Monthly

items.title: 10 — Does not meet age criteria
items.body: Class: C · Definition in Jahiz (default): Qataris 18–65, residents 21–60 [R, QIB page]; measured at maturity, so a customer fails when the months to the age limit are below minTenorMonths (12) [design default] · Likely causes: Under-age; too close to the age limit for the minimum tenor · What Jahiz does: Records; suppresses; schedules re-check on the birthday that changes the answer (under-age only) · Evidence that cures it: None · Agents · WF · POL: Raqib · WF-14 · POL-04 · Re-check: On birthday

items.title: 11 — Restricted nationality
items.body: Class: C · Definition in Jahiz (default): Nationality on QIB's restricted list; the demo ships an illustrative list that Compliance edits · Likely causes: Compliance policy · What Jahiz does: Records; suppresses. The count appears on every dashboard; the nationality detail on the record is shown to Compliance, Credit and the Head only · Evidence that cures it: None · Agents · WF · POL: Raqib · WF-14 · POL-04, POL-05 · Re-check: On list change

items.title: 12 — Eligible amount below minimum of QAR 5K
items.body: Class: C · Definition in Jahiz (default): Computed eligible amount < 5,000 · Likely causes: Low salary; obligations consume capacity; short remaining tenor to age limit · What Jahiz does: Records; shows what would change the answer (salary, obligations, tenor); no outreach · Evidence that cures it: None from the customer · Agents · WF · POL: Raqib · Muahil · WF-14 · POL-04 · Re-check: Monthly

items.title: 13 — Customer status in DB is not "Normal"
items.body: Class: A / B by sub-status · Definition in Jahiz (default): Statuses: dormant; blocked-KYC; blocked-salary-stopped; blocked-delinquency; frozen-court; frozen-sanctions; deceased; closed · Likely causes: Inactivity; expired KYC; employer termination notice; arrears; legal · What Jahiz does: Dormant → reactivation request (KYC refresh + one transaction; checker-approved status change) · blocked-KYC → WF-02/03 · blocked-salary-stopped → WF-04 · blocked-delinquency → class D · frozen/deceased/closed → Compliance, no contact · Evidence that cures it: Depends on sub-status · Agents · WF · POL: Raqib · Munadi · Mustaqbil · Fahis · Muhaddith · Muahil · WF-09 · POL-02, POL-05, POL-06 · Re-check: On status change

items.title: 14 — Finance products with irregular payments or schedules
items.body: Class: D · Definition in Jahiz (default): irregularLatePayments6m ≥ 2, or a restructured/deferred schedule (POL-05) · Likely causes: Hardship; payroll timing; standing-order failures · What Jahiz does: Suppresses offers; shows Collections; if currently past due → reason 15 path (Munabbih via WF-12); re-check after 6 regular months · Evidence that cures it: Six regular instalments · Agents · WF · POL: Raqib · WF-13 · POL-05 · Re-check: Monthly

items.title: 15 — Finance is days past due
items.body: Class: D · Definition in Jahiz (default): DPD > 0 on any finance facility · Likely causes: Missed instalment; salary delay · What Jahiz does: DPD 1–30: payment reminders inside the collections policy (one action per day, caps, hours); > 30: hand-off to Collections, Jahiz outreach stops; offers suppressed; after payment, cooling period (3 months) then re-qualify · Evidence that cures it: Payment; cooling period · Agents · WF · POL: Munabbih · Hami · Muahil · WF-12 · POL-05 · Re-check: Daily while DPD > 0

items.title: 16 — Credit card is days past due
items.body: Class: D · Definition in Jahiz (default): DPD > 0 on any card · Likely causes: Missed minimum payment · What Jahiz does: As reason 15 · Evidence that cures it: Payment; cooling period · Agents · WF · POL: as above

items.title: 17 — Has returned cheques
items.body: Class: D · Definition in Jahiz (default): Any returned cheque in the bureau record (3 years from settlement) · Likely causes: Insufficient funds; stopped cheque · What Jahiz does: Suppresses; records the settlement status; no customer message by default (the matter is criminal in Qatar and sits with Collections/Legal) · Evidence that cures it: Settlement + bureau ageing · Agents · WF · POL: Raqib · WF-13 · POL-05 · Re-check: On settlement; at 3-year ageing

items.title: 18 — Ineligible customer segment
items.body: Class: C · Definition in Jahiz (default): Staff, minors, non-resident, corporate-linked, or other segments QIB excludes · Likely causes: Segment policy · What Jahiz does: Records; suppresses · Evidence that cures it: None · Agents · WF · POL: Raqib · WF-14 · POL-04 · Re-check: On segment change

items.title: 19 — Does not meet QCB/QIB rating
items.body: Class: C · Definition in Jahiz (default): Internal rating or bureau score below threshold · Likely causes: Rating inputs · What Jahiz does: Records; suppresses; monthly re-score · Evidence that cures it: None · Agents · WF · POL: Raqib · WF-14 · POL-04 · Re-check: Monthly

items.title: 20 — AUTO_IJARA_CUT_OFF
items.body: Class: C · Definition in Jahiz (default): Product-specific model cut-off for the vehicle Ijara pre-approval. Interpretation: One Click pre-approval covers more than one product; qualify returns a result per product, R20 fails the vehicle-finance offer only, and a customer failing only R20 is eligible for personal finance. The generator applies R20 only to customers who hold or were offered vehicle finance, and the dashboard shows it under "product exclusions" · Likely causes: Model · What Jahiz does: Records the product exclusion; no outreach · Evidence that cures it: None · Agents · WF · POL: Raqib · WF-14 · POL-04 · Re-check: Monthly

items.title: Why the classes matter on the dashboard.
items.body: The 35% headline hides the real question. If, say, two thirds of fall-outs are class A and B, the bank's addressable upside is large and mostly operational; if most are class C and D, it is a credit-policy conversation. The Data health screen answers that in one tile ("X% of fall-outs are curable by a customer or bank action") because the synthetic data is generated from QIB's rank order (section 11); the same derivation runs unchanged on QIB's data once connected.

items.title: A campaign is one pre-approval run (today QIB's monthly review; in Jahiz the nightly scan, keyed by preapproval_runs.id).
items.body: A customer has at most one open case; reasons found in later runs attach to it. States are a machine in the domain package with one sub-path per class; screens never invent a state.

items.title: Class A (ask the customer):
items.body: `queued → contacted (attempt n of N) → awaiting reply → reply received → document under review → update proposed → update approved | rejected → record updated → re-qualified (eligible | still not eligible) → closed`. Side states: `paused` (hardship, complaint, dispute, opt-out handling), `escalated` (human task open), `restriction proposed → restriction approved | declined`.

items.title: Class B (bank must act):
items.body: `queued → review open (Credit | Compliance) → decided (approved | declined | reclassified) → [record updated] → re-qualified → closed`.

items.title: Class C (not eligible by policy):
items.body: `suppressed → re-check scheduled (date | event) → re-checked → closed | re-opened`.

items.title: Class D (collections boundary):
items.body: `suppressed → reminding (day n) → paid | handed over → cooling → re-qualified → closed`.

items.title: Closing codes
items.body: cured · cured-awaiting-history (the fix is in but the salary history has to accumulate) · awaiting-consent (class A, reason 8 without marketing consent) · unresponsive (attempts exhausted; restriction proposed or RM owns it) · ineligible-by-policy · opted-out · escalated-to-human · withdrawn (customer declined) · superseded. A re-opened case keeps its history.

items.title: Every transition writes a trail entry (section 15) with the actor, the autonomy rung, the policy version and clause, and — for human decisions against an agent's proposal — the…
items.body: Every transition writes a trail entry (section 15) with the actor, the autonomy rung, the policy version and clause, and — for human decisions against an agent's proposal — the override and its reason.

sections.title: Policies and procedures — the parametric model

items.title: Everything an agent is allowed to do is read from a policy, never from code.
items.body: A policy has a domain (POL-01 … POL-10), clauses with ids the assistant can cite (POL-01 §3.2), parameters, and a version with an approver and an effective date. Parameters that differ by segment are stored per segment (VVIP · HNWI · High Value · Mass); the rest are global. The engine evaluates every action against the version active at that moment and stamps the version on the trail entry. Changing a parameter is a versioned change with approval (section 4.4), not a deployment.

items.title: VVIP
items.body: QIB tier it maps to: Private Banking · Default membership rule (design default): The Private Banking flag on the record (by invitation; threshold not public) · Service model: Private banker owns every contact; Jahiz prepares, never sends

items.title: HNWI
items.body: QIB tier it maps to: Tamayuz · Default membership rule (design default): Not VVIP, and salary ≥ QAR 50,000/month or deposits ≥ QAR 350,000 [R, QIB tier page] · Service model: RM-first; Jahiz may send secure in-app messages and e-mail that the RM has approved

items.title: High Value
items.body: QIB tier it maps to: Affluent salaried below Tamayuz · Default membership rule (design default): Not HNWI, and salary ≥ QAR 20,000 or deposits ≥ QAR 100,000 · Service model: Digital-first with RM visibility; automated service messages allowed; call after two unanswered digital attempts

items.title: Mass
items.body: QIB tier it maps to: Essential Banking · Default membership rule (design default): Everyone else · Service model: Digital-first; automated service messages; contact-centre call after three unanswered attempts

items.title: Evaluated in that order, so every customer lands in exactly one segment.

sections.title: The policy domains and their parameters

items.title: Values marked come from a regulation or a published rule (research/01–02); every other value is a design default.
items.body: All are editable.

items.title: Service-message window (Doha time)
items.body: Mass: 09:00–20:00 · High Value: 09:00–20:00 · HNWI: 09:00–18:00 · VVIP: agreed with client · Basis: CRA: no direct marketing 21:00–09:00; CBUAE collections 09:00–20:00

items.title: Call window

sections.title: Procedures (the written rules the agents cite)

items.title: Each domain has 4–8 clauses in plain English and Arabic, versioned, searchable — the same search_policy pattern as Tasama HR.
items.body: Examples of clauses the assistant will cite: POL-01 §2.1 "No service message is sent outside the segment's window or inside a quiet period; a message that falls into one is rescheduled to the next window and the rescheduling is logged." · POL-02 §4.3 "A restriction is a proposal to the approver named for the segment; Jahiz never restricts an account on its own authority." · POL-06 §1.1 "No field on a customer record changes without a second person's approval; the agent is the maker." · POL-07 §3.2 "A customer who has opted out of marketing continues to receive regulatory and service messages through one neutral channel." These are synthetic procedures written to the research; QIB's own procedures replace the text when supplied, with the clause ids kept.

items.title: A change to any parameter
items.body: proposed by an authorised persona → shown as a diff against the active version with the effect preview (how many scheduled messages move, how many cases change class, how many customers would newly be suppressed or released) → approved by the approver for that domain (Head of Retail Credit for POL-01/02/03/08; Credit Policy for POL-04; Compliance for POL-05/07/09/10; Operations for POL-06) → effective immediately or on a date → every subsequent action stamps the new version. Versions are never deleted; the trail links to the version each action used. Section 9.8 describes the screen.

items.title: Ten named colleagues. autonomy is the rung the prototype runs at (A0 observe · A1 recommend · A2 acts on approval · A3 acts and reports · A4 autonomous).
items.body: None is A4. Where the rung differs by segment the table says so. Each agent has an accountable human owner (a persona, section 8).

items.title: Raqib رقيب
items.body: Title (QIB vocabulary): Data Health Monitor · Purpose: Runs the eligibility check over the whole customer base nightly and on demand, classifies every fall-out into A/B/C/D, opens or updates one case per customer, computes field-level data health · Autonomy: A3 — opens cases, never contacts anyone · Runs on Claude?: No — deterministic rules in the domain package

items.body: Title (QIB vocabulary): Co-pilot (the chat agent) · Purpose: Answers any question about the data or the actions from the same database the screens use, cites the policy clause, navigates, and prepares actions for the person to confirm · Autonomy: A2 — every write is confirmed on screen · Runs on Claude?: Yes — Claude tool-use loop on the server (section 7)

items.title: What runs on Claude and what does not, said plainly.
items.body: Five agents use Claude through Replit's Anthropic connection, for four kinds of work: Dalil's conversation, Mustaqbil's classification of free text, Fahis's reading of document images, and the free-text drafting Munadi and Muwathiq do for humans to review. Everything that decides — eligibility, classification into A/B/C/D, caps, windows, suppression, state transitions — is deterministic and testable. When the connection is absent, each Claude step has an Offline fallback and the screen says "Offline" (the Tasama HR pattern). Nothing a customer receives is composed by Claude without a human reading it first in v1.

items.title: Profile blocks on the Agents screen follow the archetype: Functions (numbered), Superpower, Business impact, Stats (live counts from the trail), tools, reads, writes, who decides.
Eighteen workflows. Each step records actor · inputs · outputs · decision, and the Workflows screen shows them as a catalogue with a walkthrough.

sections.title: Dalil — the chat agent, built exactly like Tasama HR's

items.title: The pattern being copied, stated precisely.
items.body: The two previous platforms do not work the same way. Tasama HR's Rafeeq/Murshid is a Claude tool-use loop on the server through Replit's Anthropic connection, with persona-scoped tools, policy citations, a confirm-before-write card, navigation, conversation history in PostgreSQL, a trail entry per answer, and a deterministic Offline resolver that answers the common questions from the same tools when the connection is absent. Mizan's Muhasib is the deterministic resolver only — it matches, it does not comprehend, and it says so. Mounir asked for a Claude-powered agent, so Dalil is built on the Tasama HR pattern, file for file (apps/server/src/assistant/index.ts, assistant/tools.ts, ai.ts, apps/web/src/app/assistant.tsx), with the tools and wording changed for QIB.

items.title: The rail posts { text, lang, screen } to POST /api/assistant.
items.body: The server loads the persona from the session, the last 12 messages of that persona's conversation, and builds the system prompt: who Dalil is, who the person is (persona, roles, segment scope), which screen they are on, today's date, and the rules.

items.title: If AI_INTEGRATIONS_ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is set, Claude runs a tool-use loop (max 6 turns, max_tokens 900) over the tools the persona is allowed; model chosen from the fallback list…
items.body: If AI_INTEGRATIONS_ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is set, Claude runs a tool-use loop (max 6 turns, max_tokens 900) over the tools the persona is allowed; model chosen from the fallback list claude-sonnet-4-6 → claude-sonnet-4-5 → claude-opus-4-6 → claude-haiku-4-5, the working one remembered. Every message out or blocked, every inbound classification, every proposal and decision, every policy version, every Dalil answer and confirmation writes a row. The retention rule is stated on the screen (POL-10) and export is CSV. What this does not claim: tamper evidence (hash chaining) and off-system log shipping belong to the production build, and the screen says so.

sections.title: What the prototype does not prove, said plainly

items.title: That QIB's pre-approval model would accept Jahiz's view of eligibility.
items.body: Jahiz mirrors the public QCB/QIB rules; the bank's model has inputs we do not have. The re-qualification is a rules check, not a credit decision.

items.title: That customers will respond at any particular rate.
items.body: No public benchmark exists for pre-approval remediation response or cure rates (research/02 §3 and §4); the synthetic funnel is illustrative and labelled so. The real rates come from QIB's first campaign, not from this demo.

items.title: That messages reach customers.
items.body: Every channel is simulated; delivery, bounce and push-registration behaviour are assumptions.

items.title: That Claude reads real QID and passport images at the shown confidence.
items.body: The specimens are clean renders; real photographs, glare and Arabic-only documents will perform differently, which is why v1 has no auto-approval and every write has a checker.

items.title: That the policy defaults are QIB's.
items.body: They are design defaults traced to other regulators and to practice; QIB's own procedures replace them.

items.title: That the regulatory citations are complete.
items.body: Primary QCB instruction texts could not be fetched during research; the rules are cited through secondary sources and QIB's own pages, and need confirmation against the QCB text before anything is said to QIB as a regulatory fact.

sections.title: How the platform and the customer exchange information

items.title: The question. Mock QIB app with a logged-in customer uploading documents, or e-mail with a Microsoft Graph integration — which drives the highest responsiveness for a bank in…
items.body: The question. Mock QIB app with a logged-in customer uploading documents, or e-mail with a Microsoft Graph integration — which drives the highest responsiveness for a bank in Qatar, and which demonstrates best?

items.title: What the evidence says.
items.body: 83% of QIB retail customers are digitally active and the app already lets customers update QID and passport (research/01 §6). Document upload inside an authenticated app gives the highest evidence assurance (GPG 45: capture with liveness beats an e-mailed attachment, research/02 §2.5). In-app messages and push are service communications inside an existing relationship, which sit most comfortably with the CRA rule and Law 13/2016 (research/01 §3). E-mail is the weakest retail channel in the GCC for response and the weakest for assurance (anyone can forward a photo of a card), but it is the channel the RM and the back office actually use for HNWI clients and for employer paperwork. SMS carries the nudge with a deep link into the app. WhatsApp has the highest engagement in the region but QIB has no WhatsApp channel today and it needs opt-in and templates (research/02 §1.4).

items.title: Decision. The prototype shows both, with the app as the primary channel:
A mock QIB app — "QIB Mobile (demo)"
items.body: rendered as a phone inside the platform (screen *Customer app*). The presenter picks any customer (or the scenario does) and sees that customer's phone: the push notifications Jahiz sent, the in-app secure messages, a document-upload flow (choose one of the specimen documents, or upload a real image, which Fahis reads with Claude), the One Click offer card when the customer is re-qualified, and a reply box. Everything the customer does there enters the inbound pipeline exactly as a real app event would (`POST /api/customer/...`). This is where the demo spends its time, because it is the channel that will work in Qatar.

items.title: A mailbox simulator
items.body: (screen *Communications → Mailbox*): the customer's inbox with the e-mails Jahiz sent, rendered as the customer sees them (sender identity, purpose, opt-out line in Arabic and English), and a reply composer with attachments that feeds the same pipeline. It demonstrates the e-mail channel and the RM-collected path.

items.title: Adapters, not integrations, in v1.
items.body: Push, SMS, e-mail and WhatsApp each have an adapter interface with a *simulated* implementation that writes to the customer's phone or mailbox in the prototype. A **Microsoft Graph adapter** (send through a shared mailbox, poll inbound, download attachments) is specified as the e-mail adapter's production implementation and stubbed with the environment variables it would need (`GRAPH_TENANT_ID`, `GRAPH_CLIENT_ID`, `GRAPH_CLIENT_SECRET`, `GRAPH_MAILBOX`); it is not wired live, because a demo that depends on a real mailbox and OAuth consent breaks in the room and leaks synthetic customer data into a real tenant. If QIB wants to see a real round trip, it is one adapter swap with Mounir's Microsoft 365 tenant, done after the first demo.

items.title: Why this drives responsiveness.
items.body: The customer is reached where they already are (the app), asked for exactly one thing, with one tap to upload, inside a window that respects prayer times and holidays, and told what happens next ("your offer will be restored within one working day of verification"). The reminder sequence is short because the first contact is easy to act on. The mailbox exists for the cases where a person, not an app, is the channel.

sections.title: Showing the agents at work: the Demo Director

items.title: The problem with the Tasama HR scenarios.
items.body: They ran the real engine and narrated the trail, but the screen stayed where it was and nothing showed what had changed. The audience saw beats of text, not the platform working.

items.title: Decision. Scenarios become scripted, stepped productions with a Director bar docked at the bottom of the display shell:
A scenario is a list of steps. Each step has
items.body: the narration (EN/AR), the trigger (what starts it: the nightly scan, a customer tap, an inbound e-mail, a due reminder, a policy change, a person's decision), the action the server executes (a real engine call — nothing is faked), the screen to show (and the record to open), and the changes to highlight (the server returns the ids of records it touched: cases, messages, documents, customers, trail rows).

items.title: The Director runs the step, navigates the app to the screen, opens the record, and flashes the changed rows (a highlight ring that fades over three seconds, plus a "What changed"…
items.body: The Director runs the step, navigates the app to the screen, opens the record, and flashes the changed rows (a highlight ring that fades over three seconds, plus a "What changed" list in the Director bar: "case DEMO-CASE-00412 → awaiting reply · message M-1187 sent by push · trail +2"). The presenter controls Play / Pause / Step / Back; Auto-play paces the steps at a configurable interval.

items.title: A step that needs a person (a checker's approval, an RM's send) switches persona and opens the Inbox item; the presenter can press the button in the real UI, or let the Director…
items.body: A step that needs a person (a checker's approval, an RM's send) switches persona and opens the Inbox item; the presenter can press the button in the real UI, or let the Director do it with a "(decided by the scenario)" stamp in the trail, as Tasama HR did.

items.title: The Activity console
items.body: , a drawer available on every screen, streams the engine's events as they happen (trigger → agent → action → result, with the autonomy rung and the policy clause). It is the "what are the agents doing right now" view, independent of the Director.

items.title: Triggers screen
items.body: (Agents → Triggers): every trigger type with its last firing, next firing and a *fire now* button — nightly scan, due reminders, inbound mail poll, customer app events, policy change, clock. The **virtual clock** can be advanced by a day, a week or thirty days; due reminders, escalations and T+90 restriction proposals fall out of that, which is how the demo shows time-based triggers in a minute instead of a month.

items.title: Six scenarios ship (section 12), re-cut as Director scripts.
items.body: Two run the Customer app on screen (the customer uploads; the customer replies STOP).

items.title: Running a scenario twice.
items.body: At the end of the seed, the named edge cases (and the employer under review, with its staff) are snapshotted — every core and layer row they own — into layer.snapshot_rows. When a scenario starts, the Director compares a fingerprint of its customers with the snapshot; if any of them has moved on (an earlier run of this or another scenario, the presenter clicking around, the clock), it restores exactly those records to the seeded state, writes a SCENARIO_RESET entry on each customer's trail saying so, and shows "seeded state restored" in the Director bar. Nothing else is touched: other customers, the clock, the policy version and the integration log stay as they are, so S6's policy v2 survives a re-run of S1. A full rebuild (Settings → Reset) remains the way back to the clock's starting point.

items.title: Click-through videos.
items.body: Once the app is deployed, I can drive the deployed URL with a headless browser from this environment and record each scenario as a video (and GIF) — a scripted click-through that follows the same Director steps. Give me the URL after the first Replit run and I will produce the six recordings.

items.title: Reused as they are, with the vocabulary changed
items.body: WorkflowDef with typed steps (AGENT / HUMAN / SYSTEM, each with actor, inputs, outputs, decision); the engine (startCase → advance → human step parks the case → decide resumes it; SYSTEM steps are the only writes to the core schema; savepoint per step; failed steps escalate); layer.trail with actor type, autonomy, citation, override reason; layer.integration_log in the core system's dialect; agent registry with Functions/Superpower/Impact/Stats; personas as a switcher with roles and data scope; the assistant (server tool loop, Offline resolver, Confirm card, navigate); ai.ts with Replit AI Integrations and the model fallback list; the Replit plumbing (.replit, tools/replit-run.sh, seed on first run, reset). sections.title: QIB Mobile (demo) on a real phone — Expo Go

items.title: Ask (8 October). A mock-up of the QIB Mobile app that runs in Expo Go, in the same Replit project, with the screens taken from QIB's own description of the app.
What ships. apps/mobile, an Expo SDK 57 app (React Navigation, no custom native modules, so Expo Go runs it as is).
items.body: Its structure follows qib.com.qa's "Learn about the mobile app": a customised dashboard; My Products (accounts, cards, finance, deposits); Pay & Transfer; the Smart button (net worth, Absher points, carbon footprint, relationship manager, branch booking); More (currency, cheques, requests, applications, IPO, help); Profile with My Personal Data, where the customer uploads a QID, passport or salary certificate "without visiting a branch"; notifications; and One Click Finance in the four steps QIB describes (choose, confirm, OTP + e-sign, funds). QIB's colours and logo; English and Arabic (RTL rows, Arabic strings); every record synthetic. Pay & Transfer, the Smart extras and the More services are shown and say "demo only"; everything about documents, messages and the offer is live.

items.title: How it connects. The phone talks to /api/mobile/* on the Jahiz server (CORS-open, unauthenticated: a demo).
items.body: GET /:id/home returns the customer, accounts, cards, finance, documents with expiry status, the device inbox, the open case and what it asks for, the uploads and their state, and the offer (from the latest pre-approval result). POST /:id/upload takes a camera photo (base64, read by Fahis with Claude vision) or a demo specimen and enters receive() exactly as the web shell's Customer app does; /reply, /accept-offer (amount and tenor, logged with One Click) and /read complete it. The phone polls every six seconds, so a push sent by Jahiz appears during the demo.

items.title: Replit. A second workflow, QIB Mobile (Expo Go), runs tools/replit-mobile.sh
items.body: installs apps/mobile on first run (it is a standalone package, deliberately outside the root workspaces so React Native never hoists next to the web app), sets EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL=https://$REPLIT_DEV_DOMAIN and EXPO_PACKAGER_PROXY_URL=https://$REPLIT_DEV_DOMAIN:3000, and starts Metro on 8081 (external port 3000). Two conditions on the phone's side: the development URL must not be private (Replit's "Private development URL" toggle redirects any unauthenticated client to a sign-in), and the Jahiz workflow must be up. EXPO_TUNNEL=1 switches to Expo's tunnel. The same external port in a browser serves the web build of the mock-up, the fallback on a projector. Publishing (Deployments) exposes one port only; the phone mock-up is a workspace feature for the demo, not part of the deployment.

items.title: What the video could not give.
items.body: The YouTube tour of the app could not be opened from the build environment, and the App Store page exposes no screenshots to a fetch; the screens were therefore built from QIB's written description and its public tier and feature pages, not from frames of the real UI. If QIB's own screens should be matched more closely, frames from the video are the input.
